text:
Maya: Heads-up — ran a comparsion of calibration flows today; switching our default INT8 workflow from per-tensor to per-channel calibration caused a reproducible perf regression on 4xA100 staging (seen in latency p95 for long-seq workloads).

Akshay: can you paste the profiling? is it kernel selection or runtime dispatch overhead? :thinking:

Maya: pasted below. root cause looks like two things: 1) the per-channel centroids push us to use an alternate int8 kernel (int8_channelwise_fast) that has slightly worse per-token latency but better quality; 2) calibration runtime itself increased because we do per-channel scaling over 4096 channels, and our current batching heuristic runs calibration in-process which contends with the serving runtime.

perf-bot: profiling snapshot (staging, 4xA100, batch=8, seq=1024):
```
kernel_select_time_ms: 6.7
quant_calibration_time_ms: 48.2
inference_time_ms (tokens only): 35.4
total_latency_p95_ms: 120.3
chosen_kernel: int8_channelwise_fast
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.88
```

Julia: wow quant_calibration_time is huge. are we running calibration at request time or as a precompile job?

Maya: currently in the experiment it's a deploy-time job that runs during model onboarding, but because of our autoscale/test harness it ended up on the same host as a serving shard. Need to isolate. Also calibration uses the "prod-sample-512" dataset which includes long-form 2k+ docs — outliers are skewing per-channel scales.

Liam: quick thought: per-channel helps with accuracy on rare weights but is sensitive to outliers. Do we have clipping/percentile handling? e.g., clip at 99.9 percentile before computing scales?

Akshay: we do simple max-abs by default. We have a per-tensor fallback flow that uses MSE minimization (LSQ) and 99.5 clip for some models. We could expand to hybrid: per-channel but apply symmetric percentile clipping to each channel to tame outliers.

Maya: yes — experimented with 99.9 vs 99.5: quality (logprob on eval set) improved with per-channel+99.9, but runtime calibration overhead barely changed. The big runtime hit is kernel latency for that chosen kernel. Per-channel tends to push kernel selector to the channelwise path.

Julia: then maybe improve kernel selector heuristics: pick per-channel kernel only when expected quality delta > threshold or when model sparsity/weight distribution predicts benefit. We could compute a cheap metric during calibration (e.g., per-channel kurtosis + quantization error) and store in model metadata for selector.

Maya: agreed. Proposed plan:
- enforce calibration job out-of-process / separate node pool so it doesn't contend with serving shards
- add percentile clip option (default 99.5) with per-channel toggle
- compute quick "quant-benefit" score per-layer to guide kernel selection
- fallback routing: if node latency exceeds SLO, route to per-tensor kernel variant automatically

Akshay: sounds good. small operational question: what should our default calibration dataset be? prod-sample vs curated short-turn prompts? My worry: prod-sample includes long docs that overemphasize high-magnitude weights leading to extreme scales.

Liam: I'd vote hybrid dataset: 70% short-turn conversational and 30% long-doc examples, sampled with length stratification. That prevents long-doc outliers from dominating while keeping coverage. Also preserve a small holdout of rare tokens / code snippets for tail quality.

Julia: agree on hybrid. Also add per-channel outlier detector: if a channel's max/median ratio > X, mark it for clipped calibration or use per-tensor for that layer. That reduces cross-layer perf churn (fewer channelwise kernels triggered).

Maya: implementation notes: calibration pipeline currently supports flags: --per-channel, --clip-percentile=99.5, --samples=1024. We should add --length-stratified-sampling and --benefit-threshold. Example command I'd run:
```
./calib_tool --model rwd-ggml-v2 --per-channel --clip-percentile=99.5 --samples=1024 --strata="short:0-128:0.7,long:129-2048:0.3" --emit-metrics=/tmp/calib.json
```

perf-bot: small regression alert created: #INC-2026-quant-calib-kernel-latency (linked to the perf dashboard).

Akshay: for rollout strategy, suggest canary with traffic split and per-route kernel override so we can compare quality vs p95. Also metric: tokens/sec per GPU and end-to-end p95.

Liam: one more nuance: KV cache density affects kernel perf — when KV hit-rate is high, the int8_channelwise kernel is slower because it doesn't optimize for cache reuse in our runtime yet. We should add a kernel variant int8_channelwise_kv_opt that uses fused KV loads. Longer term.

Maya: good call. I'll file a runtime task for a fused-KV kernel and meanwhile implement the hybrid calibration/data defaults + selector heuristics.

Julia: thanks — can you post the calib.json when done? puts good metadata into model registry so ops can revert if needed. :thumbsup:

Maya: will do. I'll start a short doc in eng-ml/threads with the commands and recommended defaults.

Akshay: sounds like a plan. TL;DR: per-channel -> better quality but triggers a slower kernel and heavier calibration; mitigate via dataset stratification, percentile clipping, benefit-threshold for kernel selection, and isolated calibration jobs.

Liam: +1

perf-bot: note: scheduled nightly job to re-run calibration on canary models with new defaults for 24h and emit comparison metrics.
